Critical x-values = all vertex x's plus x's of all proper (non-parallel) pairwise segment intersections; collinear-overlap and T-junction breakpoints are already vertex x's. Inside each open slab no two non-vertical edges cross, so the edges spanning the slab keep a fixed vertical order; vertical edges are measure-zero and ignored. At x_mid=(xa+xb)/2 each spanning edge's y is computed exactly and sorted. Sweeping upward from winding 0, crossing an edge adds +1 if it runs in +x direction, -1 otherwise (matches the downward-ray winding rule: a CCW unit square yields +1 inside), giving the total signed winding of ALL walks summed, not per-ring unions. A gap is filled iff w is odd (evenodd) or w!=0 (nonzero). Since the bounding lines are linear, the trapezoid area is exactly width*(y_upper(x_mid)-y_lower(x_mid)), so only mid-slab evaluations are needed. Slab areas are combined with balanced tree summation to keep rational denominators from blowing up over ~1800 slabs. Result is a reduced Fraction, formatted with no "/1" for integers.
